propositions.claim: The held GPO printing is EO 6955 of January 31, 1935.
propositions.quote: THE WHITE HOUSE January 31 , 1935 [No. 6955]

propositions.claim: The order approves an application and amends the existing code; it is amendment-only.
propositions.quote: the said Code of Fair Competition for the Automobile Manufacturing Industry be and it is hereby amended as follows

propositions.claim: Par. 1 sets the code's expiration date at June 16, 1935 or an earlier declared end of the emergency.
propositions.quote: The term ' expiration date ' as used herein means June 16 , 1935, or the earliest date prior thereto on which the President shall by proclamation

propositions.claim: Par. 2 requires overtime pay above 48 hours.
propositions.quote: Work by any employe in excess of forty -eight hours in any week shall be paid for at the rate of time and one-half for such overtime

propositions.claim: Par. 3 authorizes agreements on Fall model announcements and shows.
propositions.quote: The members of the industry are requested and authorized to enter into agreements with one another with respect to Fall announcements of new models

propositions.claim: Par. 4 confirms and continues the labor-controversy settlement machinery of March 1934.
propositions.quote: which were established by the government and have been in operation since March 1934 , and which are hereby confirmed and continued

propositions.claim: The parent code was approved August 26, 1933 under NIRA Title I.
propositions.quote: the Code of Fair Competition for the Automobile Manufacturing Industry duly approved on August 26, 1933

propositions.claim: Lead (transcription; the reviewer read the page directly and confirmed it): the 'expiration date' definition was earlier moved from December 31, 1933 to September 4, 1934 by an order of December 18, 1933.
propositions.quote: The term 'expiration date' as used herein means September 4, 1934, or the earliest date prior thereto

propositions.claim: Candidate only (transcription): EO 7076 of June 15, 1935 recites that the June 14, 1935 joint resolution extended NIRA Title I as amended; it does not name EO 6955.
propositions.quote: extends until April 1, 1936, the provisions of Title I of the National Industrial Recovery Act

propositions.claim: The current U.S. Code shows the NIRA code sections, 15 U.S.C. 703 to 712, as omitted (reviewer confirmed the page says this). This is context only; it does not name EO 6955 and proves no ending.
propositions.quote: 15 U.S. Code § 703 to 712 - Omitted

propositions.claim: Par. 2 adds a limitation: the overtime requirement does not authorize work over 48 hours where the code prohibits it.
propositions.quote: quirement shall not be construed to authorize or permit work in excess of forty -eight hours when such work is prohibited under any of the provisions of the code

propositions.claim: Candidate only (transcription, read through a fetch tool that returned the paragraph in segments): EO 7076 generally continued all existing Title I executive orders, and the agencies created under them, until April 1, 1936 so far as consistent with the amended Act, with a proviso that it does not approve or prescribe codes or provide for their enforcement. It does not name EO 6955 or the automobile code, so it neither proves continuation nor an ending of this order; it bears on the extension and labor-machinery gaps.
propositions.quote: to approve or prescribe codes of fair competition, to provide for the enforcement of such codes,

review.conclusion_reason: OPEN is justified under amendment-only rule (d): the parent code's controlling expiration provision and subsequent status remain unproved. The held definition says June 16, 1935 but does not identify what expires. Paragraph 4's continuing machinery also lacks a proved ending. Formal status is upheld only as the limited search report that no express ending was found, not proof that none exists. The basis_rule field should identify rule (d) and the unresolved own-terms-expiry inquiry under rule (b), rather than none.
missed_evidence: The held GPO printing, paragraph 2, adds: 'This requirement shall not be construed to authorize or permit work in excess of forty-eight hours when such work is prohibited under any of the provisions of the code.' This operative limitation is absent from the clause inventory and lacks its own explicit state, preventing T4.

The cited EO 7076 transcription, operative paragraph, contains a conditional general extension of existing Title I executive orders and agency activities to April 1, 1936, together with a proviso excluding code approval and enforcement authority. This is material to the extension and labor-machinery gaps, although it does not by itself resolve EO 6955 under the project's rules. Location: https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/executive-order-7076-extending-the-activities-the-nra .
review.stop_code_verdict: confirmed — the first gap concerns the parent code's operative expiration provision. The evidence slice lists held texts of EO 6955, not the parent code; the inspected government printings supply only the amended definition. WEB fits the identified external-source gap.

verdicts.reason: The held GPO printing contains the automobile-code title, January 31, 1935 date, and closing number 6955.
The held printing approves the application and immediately amends the existing code through the four numbered paragraphs.
Paragraph 1 expressly substitutes June 16, 1935, subject to an earlier presidential proclamation or congressional joint resolution declaring the emergency ended.
Paragraph 2 contains the quoted time-and-one-half requirement for work exceeding forty-eight hours weekly.
Paragraph 3 expressly requests and authorizes agreements concerning Fall passenger-model announcements and Fall automobile shows.
Paragraph 4 requires compliance with the labor-settlement provisions operating since March 1934 and expressly confirms and continues them.
The held printing's preamble confirms the August 26, 1933 approval date and Title I framework.
The cited APP page, read directly, dates EO 6513-K December 18, 1933 and prints the change from December 31, 1933 to September 4, 1934. Upheld as a transcription lead only.
The cited APP page was accessible with the www hostname. Its June 15, 1935 text confirms the quoted statutory extension and does not name EO 6955. Upheld as a candidate transcription only.
The cited hallapproved.com URL failed to open on two attempts; neither the quotation nor its context could be confirmed.

The Cornell page confirms that sections 703–712 are omitted. It does not establish the broader assertion that no current source treats EO 6955 as in force, nor provide cutoff-specific proof of that assertion.
